newsitem.title: USA: Pena says Clinton tapped him for management skills.
newsitem.headline: Pena says Clinton tapped him for management skills.

text.p: Federico Pena said Friday President Clinton asked him to run the Energy Department because of the skills he had used in running the Transportation Department during the first Clinton administration.
He said he would have to brief himself on some of the Energy Department's functions, but the two jobs had similarities.

"Essentially the President wanted me to use the same kind of management organisational skills that I used here at DOT over at DOE," Pena told reporters shortly after Clinton named him to be energy secretary.
Pena, a surprise choice for the energy post, said Clinton did not offer him the job until late Thursday afternoon.

Pena said he had talked with former White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta and Vice President Al Gore several weeks ago about whether he would be interested in running another department, "but we never had an opportunity to get down to specifics."
The chairwoman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Elizabeth Moler, had been expected to be tapped to replace Hazel O'Leary as energy secretery.
But Pena, an Hispanic, got the nod in a late effort to make the Cabinet more ethnically diverse.

"While I don't claim to understand every aspect of the Department of Energy, there have been some areas over the last five or six or seven years of my life where I've had some interaction with some of their issues," Pena said.

He cited issues such as safe transportation of nuclear materials, his efforts to promote cleaner gasoline when he was mayor of Denver, and dealings with the Energy Department over efforts to clean up the contaminated Rocky Flats nuclear weapons plant near Denver.
